title: Non-GAAP Earnings Disclosure in Loss Firms

scopes.description: Complete supplied Stata data construction and analysis workflow, retaining both packaged Perl text-search result branches, the two hand-collection rounds, the profitable-firm comparison, BCGW Table 6 Panel B, and all reported analysis sections. The packaged text-search CSVs are direct primary inputs; regenerating the revised output with the supplied Perl program is a separate conditional route because the numbered HTML working set is not supplied.

issues.description: Named WRDS products and local SAS catalog candidates remain unverified for exact measures, source period, coverage and identifier mappings. The public SEC index does not itself establish the authors’ nitem==2.02 index. EPS actual/summary candidates have bounded column probes; the catalog also lists non-EPS XEPSUS actual/summary candidates for the GPS inputs, but no probes or GPS/FPI/date-coverage checks confirm them. Monthly return/factor vintages and all lead/lag history need validation.

The quarterly main source requires lpermno, but local COMP.FUNDQ has no lpermno in the bounded field probe. A CRSP/Compustat link-table candidate exists, yet the package does not document the author’s link filters/producer or resulting fundq.dta contract.

The supplied Stata driver consumes precomputed daily size-adjusted returns with ret and decret and creates forward windows through 240 trading observations. Local raw CRSP daily returns do not establish the author’s NYSE/AMEX/NASDAQ breakpoint-adjustment product or its exact producer.
The author’s dataset page identifies the BCGW Manager Non-GAAP EPS dataset and links to a form, but the delivered file, fields, period coverage and access conditions have not been verified.

The do-file hard-codes [redacted-path-beeb72543b10], uses Windows backslash separators and alternates InFiles/Infiles and OutFiles/Outfiles. The Stata path probe showed forward slashes work and backslashes fail in this environment; configure a relative execution root and consistent path casing on a separate copy.

actions.description: Confirm the exact SEC 8-K item-index route and the author filename-to-downloadId mapping before staging items8k.dta.
steps: Check entitlement and usable coverage of the local WRDSSEC.ITEMS8K candidate for 2006–2014.
Confirm that nitem=="2.02", cik, fdate and fname follow the author’s expected definitions and that fname maps to the filing-text URL consumed by the separate Perl route.

If using a public SEC index instead, identify a documented permitted method to obtain the 2.02 item classification and reproduce the filename/downloadId join; the SEC index field list alone does not provide nitem.
Convert the confirmed rows to items8k.dta under the configured relative InFiles directory.
validation: Verify the exported columns, types, 2006–2014 period, CIK/date key uniqueness after the code filter, and expected filename-to-downloadId match before Stata execution.

actions.description: Stage the separate unadjusted IBES actuals and summary files used by the main sample and ERC branches, checking measure-specific fields and period matches.
steps: For EPS actuals and EPS summary files, the existing bounded probes support the column shapes of the ACTU_EPSUS and STATSUMU_EPSUS candidates; verify the required EPS/FPI and date coverage filters before staging those files.
For GAAP/GPS inputs, use the catalog-only ACTU_XEPSUS and STATSUMU_XEPSUS candidates as product leads. No row probes were run for them; do not transfer the EPSUS probe proof to these XEPSUS files.

Confirm that ACTU_XEPSUS provides quarterly MEASURE=GPS actuals and that STATSUMU_XEPSUS provides MEASURE=GPS/FPI=6 forecasts, including the author-required CUSIP or ticker and date fields, before preparing separate Stata files.

Apply the source filters on measure, periodicity and fiscal period only after confirming candidate values; retain announcement dates for actuals and the same-month STATPERS/FPEDATS filter for summaries.
Do not infer coverage from a single row or require original 2015/2016 byte snapshots solely from the datasheet retrieval dates.
validation: For each prepared file, inspect its own product fields, types, measure/FPI/periodicity values and date coverage; verify sample and lagged-CUSIP/date or ticker/date joins before running author code.

actions.description: Stage both monthly stock returns/prices and the separate monthly value-weighted index return used in the full sample and Table 9 portfolio branch.
steps: Check the local CRSP MSF_V2 candidate for the required monthly history and map PERMNO/MthCalDt/MthPrc/MthRet to permno/date/prc/ret in a separate preparation copy.

Retain enough prior monthly observations for the three- and twelve-month return calculations and verify the 2015–2017 period used by the later portfolio extension; the exact needed extent depends on the sample dates and constructed group index.
For crspm_vwretd.dta, confirm that the local MSIX caldt and vwretd series matches the author definition, map caldt to date, and verify monthly coverage.
Do not treat the author’s historical retrieval dates as a requirement for byte-identical files when a compatible product and history are confirmed.
validation: Check PERMNO/date keys, duplicate policy, monthly bounds and nonmissing prc/ret/vwretd in the prepared files before the Stata joins.

actions.description: Stage quarterly extensions and annual/quarterly Compustat histories used to construct future outcomes, firm age, volatility and sales growth.
steps: Use local COMP.FUNDA/COMP.FUNDQ candidates only after confirming the applicable data-product route and exact date coverage.
Build separate inputs for the 2016 future-outcome extract, the 2017 12-quarter CFO extension, annual age history, and quarterly xtravar history. Retain the keys/fields consumed by the code.

For xtravar, verify coverage from 2002 through the estimation sample and the prior four-quarter values used for growth; for extra_data files, verify up to 12 future quarter leads after the 2006–2014 sample.
Do not infer minimum endpoints solely from retrieval dates; validate the code’s explicit 2002 lower filter and future-offset requirements.
validation: Check required GVKEY/fiscal-year-quarter keys, U.S. firm/CIK/SIC fields and each source’s needed date window, then validate produced intermediate keys before merge.

actions.description: Resolve the author’s merged quarterly input contract before constructing fundq.dta; the local COMP.FUNDQ candidate lacks lpermno.
steps: Confirm whether the author-exported WRDS CRSP/Compustat Merged Fundamentals Quarterly input contains lpermno and the other columns used by the do-file, or obtain the exact documented author-prepared fundq.dta.
If a separate link-table export is proposed, obtain its documented date-effective link filters and output contract; do not infer a CCM merge recipe from the catalog link table alone.
Stage the compatible file as fundq.dta only after its identifiers, fiscal-quarter keys and required pre-sample lag history are established.
validation: Verify lpermno, gvkey, datadate, fyearq, fqtr, CIK/SIC and all code-consumed accounting fields, plus the pre-2006 quarter history used by lags.

actions.description: Resolve the prepared daily size-adjusted return file and its construction inputs for the event-return analysis.
steps: Confirm a compatible author-prepared erdport1.dta or the exact authorized WRDS SAS/SSH query and transformation that produces permno, date, ret and benchmark decret from the documented daily returns and NYSE/AMEX/NASDAQ breakpoints.
Confirm sample dates and required 61 lag / 241 future trading-observation coverage.
Do not use raw DlyRet or a monthly index as a substitute for the precomputed benchmark-adjusted return series without that source contract.
validation: Check fields, PERMNO/date uniqueness, return definitions and event-window endpoints in the prepared file before running Step 1b.

actions.description: Confirm a monthly four-factor source compatible with the author’s Table 9 joins and prepare it under ff_factors_4.dta.
steps: Confirm local FF.FACTORS_MONTHLY or the official Fama/French 3-factor and Momentum files cover the portfolio regression months with compatible units and month keys.
Check the historical definition expected by the 2017 author file; the official library documents a FIZ-to-CIZ source-format change beginning January 2025 and offers historical files.
Map the required date and mktrf, smb, hml, umd fields to the author’s Stata input without changing the regressors.
validation: Verify all four factor fields, units, monthly key alignment and complete span of the joined portfolio regressions.

actions.description: Obtain and verify the BCGW comparison file used by the supplied Table 6 Panel B branch.
steps: Use the author’s Manager Non-GAAP EPS Dataset page and its linked access form to determine delivery and access conditions.

Verify the delivered dataset corresponds to Bentley, Christensen, Gee and Whipple (JAR 2018), covers 2003–2016, and includes gvkey, datadate, MGR_NG_EPS and mgr_exclude (plus url as dropped by the source).
Convert to the Stata input bcgw_2018_ng_data_2003to2016.dta after confirming its period and keys.
validation: Check fields, coverage, GVKEY/date keys and the resulting join cardinality before the BCGW branch runs.

actions.description: Add a compatible rbounds Stata command for the supplied sensitivity-analysis branches.
steps: Obtain and install the rbounds Stata ado package through an authorized Stata package source.
Make the command discoverable on the Stata adopath used by the execution copy.
validation: Run which rbounds in Stata 18 and confirm that it resolves to the intended command before running Table 8.

actions.description: Create a configured execution copy with relative paths and the package helper directory first on the Stata adopath.
steps: Copy the supplied package to a separate execution directory with coherent InFiles, OutFiles and EDGAR directories.

In the copy only, set the root global to a relative root such as "."; convert all path separators to forward slashes and normalize Infiles/Outfiles spellings to InFiles/OutFiles consistently across producers and consumers.
Prepend the bundled helper directory with adopath ++ "ado" so the supplied cluster2, logit2, psmatch2 and konfound files are found ahead of other versions.
Keep executable configuration paths relative or under [redacted-path-1843e3452e62]; do not set the root to the Dropbox workspace path.
validation: From the configured execution directory, run harmless Stata file-open checks using a relative forward-slash path, then use which to verify the four packaged ADO paths and the three invoked helpers.
After all inputs and software are ready, launch the complete driver in Stata batch mode from the configured copy; retain all analysis branches and inspect generated output/logs for missing inputs.

actions.description: Use the complete supplied Stata driver after the input and software actions close their current gaps.
steps: Complete the relative-path configuration and stage the inputs under the named directories.
Ensure Stata resolves the package ADOs and rbounds before execution; if regenerating text-search output, also stage the numbered HTML files and File::Slurp.

Run lv_jar_stata_code.do in Stata 18 batch mode from the configured copy so Steps 1–12, both hand-collected rounds, profit comparison, BCGW Panel B, ERC, sensitivity and portfolio branches run in source order.
validation: Confirm that every expected producer output exists before its next consumer, both search CSV joins use the generated downloadId mapping, all analysis branches complete, and lv_jar_dataset.dta is produced with the documented share fields.

review_notes: The EDGAR/downloadlist.txt file was treated as data. Only the frozen inventory size/hash were used; no line contents were read as narrative.

The supplied Perl source was statically inspected from the actual package file even though the frozen source reader did not cache it. A hashed JSON records its local HTML input/output interface. The HTML presentation copy is not treated as a second program.

The hand-collected DTA files and both text-search CSV outputs are accepted as author-prepared primary inputs. This avoids making the historical collection/download path a mandatory dependency where the Stata driver consumes supplied outputs.

The final lv_jar_dataset.dta is a sharing/output dataset with identifiers, text-search and hand-coded variables; its probe and variable list do not support a separate analysis-only scope that reproduces the paper analyses.

Source and software checks were static or bounded metadata probes only. No author code, model regressions, dataset imports into author software, installation or downloads were performed. execution_verified remains false.

Optional, unselected Perl regeneration lead: static inspection shows the supplied program reads numbered local HTML via File::Slurp and writes output_new.csv; the Perl runtime is present and File::Slurp is absent. The primary Stata workflow directly consumes the two verified packaged text-search CSVs, so the Perl module and HTML handoff are not mandatory for this target. If the regeneration route is selected later, stage the numbered HTML files in its working directory, prepare File::Slurp, and verify the output_new.csv File_Number/word schema against the Stata download IDs.
